translations.text: Opposite the ark of the Lord. David had brought it up from the town of the villagers to the place David had prepared for it, for he had pitched a tent for it in Jerusalem.
And now, Lord my God, let the words you spoke to David my father be fulfilled, for you have established me over this people, who are as numerous as the dust of the earth.
The king made silver as plentiful as stones in Jerusalem, and cedars as abundant as the sand on the seashore.
He made two pillars in front of the great house, eighteen cubits tall, and the capitals on their tops were five cubits high.
He made the cast-metal sea, ten cubits from rim to rim, square all around, and five cubits high. A cord thirty cubits long encircled it on all sides.
The priests brought the ark of the Lord and set the ark in its place in the Holy of Holies, beneath the wings of the cherubim.
The cherubim were spread out over the place of the ark, and the cherubim covered the ark and its poles from above.

There was nothing in the ark except the two stone tablets that Moses had placed there, which he had brought down from Mount Sinai. This was the covenant that the Lord gave the Israelites when they came out of the land of Egypt.

And now, Lord of lords of Israel, keep for your servant David my father what you promised him: 'You will never lack a son before me to sit on the throne of Israel, provided that your sons take care in their conduct to walk before me according to my laws, as you walked before me.'

Also concerning the foreigner who is not from your people Israel and comes from a distant country because of your name—for they will hear the fame of your great name, your mighty hand, and your uplifted arm—and they come and pray before you on that day in this house.
They will pray before you and turn back, and in the countries of their captors they will say, 'We have sinned, provoked anger, and done wrong.'

On the day of [?] in the month of Tishri, the king sent the people away. The people blessed the king and went to their towns, rejoicing and glad at heart, giving thanks and praise for all the good things the Lord had done for David his servant, for Solomon his son, and for Israel his people.
I will scatter you from the land I gave you, and this house, which I consecrated to my name, I will uproot from before me. Israel will become a proverb and a tale among all the nations.

They will say, 'Because they abandoned the covenant of the Lord, the God of their ancestors, who brought them out of the land of Egypt, and went and revered the gods of the nations, served them, and bowed down to them. That is why the Lord brought these calamities upon them.'
She said to King Solomon, 'The report I heard in my country about your words and your wisdom was true.'
For King Solomon had ships that went to Tarshish with Hiram's servants. Once every three years they returned, and the ships that went to Tarshish carried silver, gold, elephants, apes, and peacocks.
They bought horses for Solomon from Egypt and from all the countries.
King Rehoboam consulted the elders who had served his father Solomon while he was alive. He said to them, 'What answer do you advise us to give this people?'
Thus says the Lord: 'Do not go up and do not fight. Return, each man to his home, for this matter has come from me.' They listened to the word of the Lord and turned back, each going to his home.
He did what was evil before the Lord and did not set his heart on revering the Lord and seeking him with all his heart.
The Israelites fled before the people of Judah.
Abijah inflicted a great slaughter on them, and five hundred thousand young men of Israel fell.
He removed the high places and idols from all the towns of Judah. His kingdom was at rest in his days, and he had no enemy among any of his neighbors.
They gathered in Jerusalem in the third month of the fifteenth year of Asa's reign.
His heart grew strong in the ways of the Lord, and he also removed the altars and high places that were within the territory of Judah.
All these served King Jehoshaphat, apart from those whom the king put in charge of the fortified towns throughout the land of Judah.

The king of Israel gathered the prophets, about four hundred men, and said to them, “Shall we go to battle at Ramoth-gilead or not?” They said to him, “Go up, and the Lord will deliver your enemies into your hands.”
When the chariot commanders saw that Jehoshaphat was not the king of Israel, they turned back from pursuing him.
He appointed judges in the land, in all the fortified towns of Judah and in the strong towns.

The spirit of courage from the Lord rested upon Hazael son of Zechariah, son of Benaiah, son of Jehoiada, son of Mattaniah, a Levite from the descendants of Asaph, while he was standing before the people of Israel.
The Levites from the descendants of Kohath and the descendants of Korah stood up to praise the Lord, the God of Israel, with a loud voice.
They came to Jerusalem with songs of praise, harps, and curved and straight horns, and they came to the house of the Lord.
The rest of Jehoshaphat’s deeds, from first to last, are written in the accounts of Jehu son of Hanani, which are recorded in the book of the kings of Israel.
He also made high places in the hill country of Judah, gave wine to Jerusalem’s Nazirites to drink, and scattered the people of Judah.

He returned to Jezreel to recover from the wound they had inflicted on him at Ramoth while he was fighting Hazael king of Edom. Ahaziah went down to see Joram son of Ahab in Jezreel because he was ill.

The Levites and all the people of Judah did as Jehoiada the priest had commanded them. Each man took his companions, those who were on guard duty when the Sabbath began together with those who were on guard duty when the Sabbath ended, because Jehoiada the priest had released them from their guard duties.
They brought out the king’s son and put the crown and [?] on his head, and established him as king. Jehoiada and his sons anointed him and said, “Long live the king!”
Joash was seven years old when he became king, and he reigned for forty years in Jerusalem. His mother’s name was Zibiah, from the city of Beersheba.
Jehoiada took two wives for him, and he fathered sons and daughters.
Jehoiada grew old and lived a full life, and he died at the age of one hundred and thirty.

Although the men who came with the army of Edom were few, the Lord delivered a very large army into their hands because they had abandoned the Lord, the God of their ancestors. The judges rejected what Joash had done.

When they departed from him, having left him seriously ill, his servants plotted against him because of the blood of the sons of Jehoiada the priest. They killed him on his bed, and he died. They buried him in the city of David his ancestor, but they did not bury him in the burial place of the kings.
He did what was right before the Lord, just as David his ancestor had done.
He said to him, “This position does not belong to you, O king, nor is it proper for you to offer incense on the altar.”

At that moment King Uzziah became angry with the priests and ordered that they be removed from the sanctuary. At that very moment leprosy came out of the sanctuary and fell upon King Uzziah’s forehead as he entered to offer incense in the house of the Lord.
He did what was right before the Lord, just as David his ancestor had done.
King Hezekiah rose early, gathered the elders of Jerusalem, and entered the house of the Lord.

He stationed the Levites in the house of the Lord with songs of praise to the sound of harps, with the songs of praise of David, and with the songs of praise of Gad, King David’s prophet, and of Nathan, King David’s prophet. For David sang the praises of the Lord his God according to what came from the mouths of the prophets.

He spoke to Azariah the chief priest, from the house of Zadok, and said to him, “You are permitted to eat this firstfruits offering, because it has entered the house of the Lord. Eat and be satisfied, and give what remains of it to the poor and the needy, because the Lord has blessed his people and given them this abundance.” They gave what remained to all the people of Israel.
Hezekiah ordered that chambers be prepared in the house of the Lord, and they prepared them.
Oil and wine were given to the priests and the Levites according to their ancestral households, from twenty years old and upward, according to their duties and their divisions.
And they will strengthen themselves and build a wall opposite another wall, and fill in the ditch that David made. Hezekiah made many weapons, shields, and spears.
This is what Sennacherib king of Assyria says: On whom are you relying as you remain under siege in Jerusalem?
Hezekiah had very great wealth and honor. He made storehouses for silver, gold, precious stones, spices, pearls, and highly desirable objects.
Amon was twenty-two years old when he became king, and he reigned in Jerusalem for two years.
They handed it over to the workers who supervised the LORD’s house, and they gave the money to the workers in the LORD’s house to repair and restore the building.
They gave it to the carpenters, the builders, and those buying good [?] and timber to repair and restore the building that the kings of Judah had dismantled.
While they were bringing out the money that had come into the LORD’s house, Hilkiah the priest found the book of the LORD’s law that had been given through Moses.
When the king heard the words of the law, he tore his clothes.

Hilkiah and all those whom the king had sent went to Huldah the prophetess, the wife of Shallum son of Tikvah, son of Hadhas, the keeper of the garments. She lived in Jerusalem, in the school. They spoke with her as the king had commanded.
Prepare your hearts and the hearts of your fathers, according to what David king of Israel wrote and what his son Solomon wrote.
The Israelites who were present celebrated the Passover at that time, and the Festival of Unleavened Bread for seven days.
And the rest of Josiah’s deeds and his acts of kindness, in accordance with what is written in the LORD’s law.
Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon came up against him and bound him in chains to take him to Babylon.
Nebuchadnezzar brought some of all the furnishings of the house to Babylon and placed them in his temple in Babylon.
The LORD, the God of their fathers, sent word to them through his messengers, early and late, because he had compassion on his people and on the flock he had chosen.

This is what Cyrus king of Persia says: The LORD, the God of heaven, has given me all the kingdoms of the earth, and he has commanded me to build him a house in Jerusalem, which is in Judah. Who among you belongs to all the people and is favored by the LORD his God? Let him go up and come to me.
